      "observations": [
        "All 102 owned lines across production and browser-test files were read. A location selector handler prevents default navigation and calls the imported external-link helper. Actual dispatch finds the closest matching selector but passes the original event; this handler uses event.target.href. Returning false from that handler is not a substitute for its explicit preventDefault call.",
        "The actual location setter parses trimmed text but uses the original location for displayed text/href; it is not an HTTP-only validator. The checked helper performs URI creation, optional history and protocol-dependent permission/principal handling, then calls the external protocol service. No native handler or security-policy result was executed.",
        "The test replaces the HTTPS fixture URI with an existing chrome test-directory URI, installs a beforeunload failure guard and removes that listener before deliberate cleanup. It arms the external-service mock promise before the synthetic click and directly compares the captured URI; that proves the intended static assertion path, not actual OS browser launch.",
        "The changed final Assert.equal(await loadPromise, URI) has no message; its adjacent text/href checks and unload guard have nonempty expected-behavior messages. Missing should alone in another author's message is not a defect. The new complex multiline import is directly followed by a distinct loading-policy comment without a separating blank line; a blank line would make those steps clearer under the current deliberate readability rule.",
        "Existing location rendering/navigation-phase knowledge is reused instead of copying its broad analysis. No live location click, accessibility or browser test ran.",
        "Complete Bug 2014108 current 0–2/activity/footer and full D284131 creation-to-close timeline, including expanded older changes, were read. There are no actual inlines or summary edits. The reporter asks to open the inert location link; the revision has sparse acceptance, a Try locator, remote completion and an explicit like-to-link title correction.",
        "Actual source supplies default prevention plus external-helper dispatch and a browser unload guard. Text/href and mocked URI assertions are direct source expectations, distinct from an OS handler or permission result. The final dispatch comparison still lacks a message; sparse acceptance does not resolve that source finding.",
